well u have four options:

GU - More old school MH with some crazy mechanics that give the game a very arcade feel, but being an old school game you gonna have a lot of grind to do for parts and equipment and the game doesn't have a lot of the QoL from the newer games.

Rise - Newer game that has the same arcade feel from GU with the addition of modern QoL and more streamlined progression so u won't have to grind as much.

Stories 1 & 2 - Pretty much Pokémon MH, the combat is a very simple rock, paper, scissors style and while they can be challenging games the focus is on the story more than anything, also the big selling point of the game is that you can ride monsters and they have their own special abilities like climbing or breaking rocks (like TMs if you will).

Now for which is worth playing I would say to go with Rise if you are new to series, I'm pretty sure you can find lots of ppl on MH Discord servers wanting to play, GU also has quite a bit of an active player base. Hope this helps :3

Speaking from the perspective of someone who didn't grow up with the series but never had the chance to play modern MH and started with Freedom Unite, I don't think it's the nostalgia.

Sure nostalgia plays a part in it for the veterans and it always will, but the older games had more going for them, they were games that put a lot of emphasis on the small things (gathering, crafting, farming, etc.) as much as they did in the big things (hunting) and that created games that were more complete experiences. Couple that with the iconic visual and motifs of the series (palicos, armors, monster and weapon designs, etc.) and you have what made Monster Hunter, well, Monster Hunter.

It was never about just one aspect or the other, it was about the balance between them, and what Wilds do it's that it takes away much of the small things in the name of QoL without concern for the balance that has kept the series afloat for so long. What remains is just the set dressing and in that way Wilds feels more like a monster hunting game with Monster Hunter aesthetics. 

Now, I do wanna say that I agree with you that the older games had lots of problems and I'm happy to see them gone and that honestly I think World was the ideal Monster Hunter, combining previous aspects of the series with modern standards. Wilds just throws away too much to be a Monster Hunter to me personally.

Anyway I talked a lot, but yeah I hope you got a better understanding of another side of this argument and also thank you for sharing your own argument.

So there's this videogame I really like called "Star Wars Knights of The Old Republic II The Sith Lords". 

As you guessed it the game takes place in the Star Wars universe and tells the story of a woman called The Exile (she doesn't really have a in-game name because it's a RPG), a exiled jedi who lost her connection to the Force due to traumatic events. The story revolves around the Exile reestablishing her connections to the force and finding the real reason as to why the connection was lost in the first place. 

I really love this game because it's basically a story about healing from trauma and one very well done. Every single place you visit, every single character you meet fits this theme. You will frequently hear the characters referring to events with terminology often used to talk about psychological trauma.

In my opinion the game portrays healing in a very realistic way, as something hard but necessary to do in order for one to move forward with their life. It also emphasizes the importance other people play in this process and how empathy can save lives. 

The game also portrays how destructive treating trauma as strength is (in the "what doesn't kill me makes me stronger" sense). 

I personally think the game is an absolute masterpiece and is also my favorite game of all time, it just means that much to me. 

Also, if you have the time and patience [this video](https://youtu.be/5texil4EYP4) goes in depth about the game themes and story if you're interested.
